label: r4c3
name: Deeper trunk with whole-board context
hypothesis: New idea on top of r3c1: a third residual block, plus a pooled summary of the whole board added as extra input channels to the head, and the learned output weights from the first candidate. Choosing a safe placement order (for example, filling cells under an overhang first) needs information from beyond a 7x7 receptive field. The compute ratio is about 1.5, so fewer samples. Refuted if it does not beat r3c1's 0.11.
last_analysis: r3c1 is the only trial with any successes. It sums the placement output over all 8 flips and transposes of the grid and scored 0.111 (0.078 and 0.145 on its two seeds). r3c3 used the same network and recipe with only the described action layout and scored 0.000. So the action layout probably differs from the description by a flip or transpose. Every trial without the flipped and transposed outputs scored 0, whatever the recipe or capacity, so those earlier zeros say little about recipes or network size. Training success (0.12) is close to dev success, which suggests the network is underfitting rather than overfitting. r3c1 trained in only 28 seconds. All three candidates keep the flipped and transposed outputs and change one thing each: a learned weight on each output so the wrong orientations can be switched off quickly, a recipe that gives more credit to the exact-build bonus, and a third residual block plus whole-board context in the head.
